subject.title: Add a retraction window for forwarded exec approvals (agent-cancellable hold before prompt delivery)

question: Should OpenClaw add a core opt-in forwarded exec-approval hold/retract mechanism, and which surface should own agent-originated retraction plus audit and fail-open/fail-closed semantics?
rationale: The request is plausible but changes approval timing, public config, Gateway RPC shape, and dependency/native approval contracts; implementation should not proceed until maintainers choose the product and security boundary.

options.title: Design core hold/retract
options.body: Keep this issue open and require a maintainer-approved design for `holdMs`, retraction authorization, audit records, delivery failure behavior, and Codex/native mappings before code changes.

options.title: Defer to immediate approvals
options.body: Reject or defer the feature and keep current immediate forwarding semantics to avoid adding more approval protocol surface.

options.title: Narrow to non-protocol UX
options.body: Explore smaller prompt-deduping or model-guidance mitigations without adding an agent-accessible retraction RPC.

recommendation.title: Design core hold/retract
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open and require a maintainer-approved design for `holdMs`, retraction authorization, audit records, delivery failure behavior, and Codex/native mappings before code changes.

likelyOwner.reason: This handle has the strongest recent current-main history across Gateway approval forwarding, routing, and security hardening paths touched by the design.
